I've been formalizing results related to the current status of the Inverse Galois Problem. Besides formalizing several finite simple groups (Mathieu groups and their friends), I also have the rigidity method (i.e. suitable tooling to verify the certificate for a large class of other interesting groups), and Shafarevich's theorem that all solvable groups can be solved in the IGP. The rigidity method required a particular (weak) version of the Riemann existence theorem (see #mathlib4 > Riemann's Existence Theorem for P^1 ), and Shafarevich required a decent chunk of class field theory.

https://github.com/Timeroot/InverseGaloisProblem

This project started when I heard the early rumors that people were working seriously on getting M23 in there. Ironically, that one is still not done, because it doesn't go through the typical rigidity method exactly; and verifying the explicit polynomial requires some tools for efficiently working with discriminants etc. that are very different type of effort. (Although I think results coming out of this challenge will be very useful there!)

If you’re looking for more theorems related to the IGP, formalizing (the proof of) the geometric Shafaravich conjecture might be a nice milestone. The statement is simple enough to write down as a lean-eval challenge.
The proof of Abhyankar’s conjecture would also be a nice target.

I noticed that https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/main/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/ThricePuncturedSphere/Classification.lean exists in TauCeti. But isn't the API overly restrictive? Why not generalize to arbitrary number of points and choice of points (not just 0, 1)? Looks a bit problematic that this passed AI review.

Junyan Xu said:

Looks a bit problematic that this passed AI review.

Yep, TauCeti review definitely isn't perfect. Maybe it would be a good idea to start making a list of expert-authored issues in TauCeti so that we can use it to improve agent review in the future.

@Junyan Xu I agree. But perhaps worth mentioning that the thrice punctured P1 is “special” because of Belyi’s theorem, so if this is part of a larger development in TauCeti, it would be more understandable. Not sure if this is the case though
It's likely this is part of this roadmap on Belyi maps, dessins d'enfants, and three-point covers
